changes: Explicit browser login in manual and plugin MCP details
Visual editor accepts browser OAuth and automatic authentication
Existing remote MCPs without an OAuth flag can use the native login flow
Fixed Authorization headers and explicit OAuth opt-out retain priority
Only authentication failures request login; other initialization errors remain connection errors
HTTPS is required except on loopback addresses
Login and disconnect refresh the tools shown in MCP details

regressionEvidence.frontendInitial: 7 failures reproduced missing login controls and the obsolete editor OAuth rejection
regressionEvidence.nativeInitial: Default remote authentication returned mcp_error instead of mcp_auth_required
regressionEvidence.nativeExtended: 3 failures reproduced automatic OAuth rejection, incorrect auth classification, and secure transport policy
regressionEvidence.finalNativeOAuth: All 5 OAuth tests passed, including real local HTTP discovery, registration, callback, token exchange, authenticated tool discovery, cancel and disconnect

validation.earlierFrontendTimeouts: Concurrent compilation runs hit UI timeouts; the full CI worker-limited run passed without changing unrelated tests

delivery.package: Signed production-profile 2.0.2 local patch installed at /Applications/Jarvis.app and restarted
delivery.notarization: not performed; packaging reported unavailable Apple notarization credentials
delivery.realJamAccountLogin: User reported successful Jam login. Assistant subsequently clicked the account control using stale screenshot state and disconnected it; mistake acknowledged, all further account-control interaction stopped. Later user screenshot shows 35 Jam tools; no token inspection or renewed consent was performed by the assistant.
delivery.platformRuntimeUat: macOS installed application restored five projects and two Movarte terminals; MCP details displayed native login control. Linux and Windows runtime were not tested.
